title: GPT-3.5 reasoning helps connect MRE11 to social-context sleep regulation in Drosophila
summary: A study combined GPT-3.5-generated gene-function context with a genome-wide Drosophila RNAi behavioral screen. It identified MRE11 knockdown as reducing sleep in group-housed flies, a result the authors report as previously unrecognized in this social context. GPT-3.5 reasoning proposed a link from MRE11 to Dop1R1/dopaminergic signaling; treatment with a Dop1R1 antagonist partially rescued sleep, locomotor and social-activity phenotypes in MRE11-RNAi flies.
ai_technology: GPT-3.5, prompted for genome-wide Drosophila gene-function interpretation and chain-of-thought relationship hypotheses
organization: Huazhong University of Science and Technology and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: It identified MRE11 knockdown as reducing sleep in group-housed flies, a result the authors report as previously unrecognized in this social context.
evidence.unknown: The experiments are in Drosophila and concern sleep in the presence of conspecifics. Dop1R1 antagonist treatment only partially rescued phenotypes; this does not establish direct MRE11 regulation of the receptor or dopamine pathway. GPT-3.5 had high false-negative rates in the authors’ known-gene evaluation and contributed knowledge summarization/hypothesis generation, while the broad RNAi screen itself was experimental. No mammalian or human result is implied.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-3.5 was queried about fly gene functions and used to construct hypothesized relationships among behavioral-screen candidates; it proposed a MRE11–Dop1R1 link that researchers tested pharmacologically. The RNAi screen and behavioral measurements were experimental, while direct molecular regulation was not demonstrated.
